title: Alternate Path μ-op Cache Prefetching
problem: Datacenter applications with large code footprints cause μ-op caches to become over-subscribed; the μ-op cache has lower reach than the instruction cache and is not filled speculatively, making naive prefetching ineffective.
motivation: Improving frontend efficiency and instruction delivery performance in datacenter processors constrained by large code footprints.
method: The system identifies conditional branches (if-then-else decision points) where the CPU's prediction is least confident. When found, it speculatively prefetches the micro-operations (individual CPU steps) from the opposite execution path into the μ-op cache, preparing for a potential misprediction. The approach uses small extra prediction circuits, requiring only 8.95-12.95 KB of additional storage.
key_novelty: Preemptively loading alternate code paths into the μ-op cache for branches the CPU struggles to predict, hedging against mispredictions.
contributions: Analysis showing naive μ-op cache prefetching fails due to over-subscription pressure in datacenter workloads
Identification of pipeline refills as critical execution points where μ-op cache prefetching delivers meaningful gains
Alternate path prefetching mechanism using branch predictor confidence to identify hard-to-predict branches without extra state
Hardware implementation with minimal overhead (8.95-12.95 KB) achieving 1.9-2% average speedup and up to 12% on CVP-1 traces

metrics.speedup: 1.9-2% average, up to 12% on CVP-1 traces
